1#_: For prohibition of eating. And even not in the manner of eating and benefit it is forbidden and one would receive lashes for it, unlike other prohibitions except kilaei hakerem — so Rambam chapter 14 Laws of Forbidden Foods; Pri Megadim brought this in the introduction.
2#_: For prohibition of benefit. And if one would receive lashes for benefit — Rambam's view is that one does not receive lashes, and other poskim hold that one does receive lashes; the practical difference today is whether one receives lashes. Beit HaTaharah above siman 16 s.k. 10. And see Pri Megadim in the introduction that he was uncertain whether chelev shemen is forbidden in cooking and benefit d'oraisa — for in eating we hold chelev shemen is forbidden d'oraisa, and for cooking and benefit it is uncertain — see there. And see Tzalach in Pesachim daf 22 s.v. and behold a nursing mother — he was also uncertain regarding this for benefit alone, and afterward wrote plainly that according to Rambam one certainly does not receive lashes for benefit, and therefore regarding prohibition, chelev shemen is also forbidden for benefit d'oraisa; but for other poskim who receive lashes for benefit, one certainly does not receive lashes for benefit except for a kezayit — see there. And see in responsum of Rabbeinu Akiva Eiger siman 195 that he brought proof from the sugya in Bava Kamma daf 41 that its measure is in benefit of a perutah — see there. And basar b'chalav that becomes forbidden for benefit — one buries it. And if one burned it, its ash is also forbidden for benefit d'oraisa. And regarding whether it is permitted to feed it to dogs — see below siman 94 s.k. 5.
3#_: By way of cooking. Beit HaTaharah — and see Peri Chadash that frying is also included in cooking; but Magen Avraham in Seder Limud general rule 5 and Maharam Schiff at end of the book on Chullin inclined to be lenient that frying is not included in cooking and is not forbidden for benefit. And in Peri Megadim one may be lenient. And hot in hot without gravy — Pri Megadim wrote in the introduction in name of Rashal that it is not by way of cooking and is permitted for benefit — see there. [And see in responsum Chasam Sofer siman 97 what he wrote in our time; nevertheless even in these that are only d'rabbanan and permitted for benefit one must give them to a non-Jew thus and not cook initially, for then one violates cooking and it is forbidden for benefit d'oraisa, for although the piece absorbed not by way of cooking, nevertheless afterward the meat cooked with the milk absorbed in it — this is obvious; and so in responsum Noda Biyehudah Yoreh Deah siman 26 s.v. and from this.]
4#_: For benefit. Beit HaTaharah — and see in responsum Shaar Efraim siman 38 that he ruled regarding butter that was cooked in a pot of meat in a kli rishon — forbidden to light with it to illuminate the house because it is forbidden for benefit; and also to light Chanukah lights — although mitzvot are not for benefit, nevertheless forbidden since for Chanukah one needs a measure, and in basar b'chalav since forbidden for benefit the measure is broken — see there (see Pri Megadim that he copied in his name that for Chanukah it is permitted, and Maharam Chagiz did not examine there well; and so in responsum Orach Chaim siman 573 in his name that for Chanukah too it is forbidden). And see in responsum Shamayim Rosh siman 285 in Hagahot Kesef Nivchar there what he wrote on words of Shaar Efraim; and see in Or Zaru'a in Orach Chaim there that he wondered — behold in any case it is forbidden because of cooking basar b'chalav. And see in responsum Shvut Yaakov part 1 siman 38 and in his responsum there what he wrote; and see in responsum Rabbi Akiva Eiger in omissions to siman 84.
5#_: In meat. See Maharam Schiff at end of Chullin that he wrote regarding liver that they wanted to fry it in fat and fried it in butter and inclined to be lenient — liver is blood and "kid" the Torah forbade, not blood (he also inclined there that frying is not cooking). And see Pri Megadim that wrote that for this alone one certainly should not rely and be lenient based on "kid" and not blood; and Maharam Schiff did not write this except as a mere side point. And see in responsum Shamayim Rosh siman 285 in Hagahot Kesef Nivchar there what he wrote on words of Maharam Schiff.
6#_: Impure. See in Derech Mitzvosecha that he wrote: nevelah meat and likewise milk — forbidden to cook in milk d'oraisa and one receives lashes for cooking it; but for eating there is no basar b'chalav prohibition — all this is explained in Rambam chapter 9 Laws of Forbidden Foods law 6. However whether it is forbidden for benefit is not explained there, but in commentary on Mishnayot chapter 3 of Keritut it is explained that it is not forbidden for benefit; and although according to Tosafot in Chullin 101 s.v. inclusive prohibition that they wrote that prohibition of benefit is not called an additional prohibition — there is no necessity for Rambam's words there; nevertheless we do not find that Tosafot in their explanation disagree with Rambam's ruling that where there is no eating prohibition because of basar b'chalav, there is no benefit prohibition; therefore one who relies on this in a case of loss should not lose — end. And see Pri Megadim in the introduction that wrote that we rule it is forbidden for benefit d'oraisa — see there. (And see in responsum Chasam Sofer siman 92 that they also asked on this matter and brought words of the Gaon Me'il Tzedakah in Kanfei Yonah siman 87 regarding an incident where craftsmen mixed butter into milk to make candles because milk was expensive and he inclined to forbid it for benefit; although from the reason of tarbus one may say that candles of milk are not made only from kidney and abdominal milk that they mix many types of milk and membranes that have no karet — if so there is basar b'chalav because of mixture of these milks; but nevertheless because of nevelah there is concern, for most animals of non-Jews are not slaughtered, and nevertheless the Gaon forbade for benefit — if so he holds that although there is no eating prohibition, nevertheless there is benefit prohibition. He expanded on this and concludes that certainly the rabbi who ruled is like the Gaon Kanfei Yonah; and so it appears from many great Acharonim. And even for Derech Mitzvosecha he does not deal with benefit of lighting; but a kreuzel candle to light by hand — there is concern for cooking basar b'chalav because the drop around the flame cooks; and although for Shabbat this is not considered cooking, for basar b'chalav it may be cooking. He also wrote: however a kreuzel candle that became forbidden as above and was mixed with others — plainly nullified, for this is not davar sheb'minyan, only specifically Chanukah lights where each night they count the number of lights for its mitzvah — see there. And see in responsum Shvut Yaakov part 1 siman 60.)
7#_: And meat of wild animal and fowl, etc. And likewise the reverse — meat of pure domestic animal in milk of pure wild animal is not forbidden d'oraisa. Tiferet Lemoshe — see there.
8#_: Permitted in cooking. See in Chumdei Daniel 18 that he wrote that it is permitted to cook meat for a non-Jew in a pot of milk — it is not a kli rishon, for whatever is forbidden only d'rabbanan they did not decree on cooking and benefit; and here there is no marit ayin — who would know whether it is a pot of meat or milk? Nevertheless one should be stringent because Rama wrote in seif 6 that it is forbidden to stoke, etc. And one may say because initially it was pure milk they were somewhat stringent — see there.
9#_: Prohibition. Beit HaTaharah — and see in responsum Chinuch Beit Yosef siman 61 that he supports words of Levush that it is forbidden to eat fish in milk because he investigated with expert physicians that specifically fish fried with butter is permitted to eat, but fish cooked in milk there is danger of illness — fish cool very much and milk is bad and harmful to the body — see there [and see in responsum Chasam Sofer siman 101 that wrote this is not true and we rely on Rambam, the great of physicians]. And so Pri Megadim in name of BeHag that fish with milk is dangerous, and in butter and fat absorbed on the milk there is no danger — see there, that it appears his view is that even with milk specifically l'chatchila one should be careful, but b'dieved one should not forbid. And see in responsum Adnei Paz siman 42 that wrote in name of Rabbeinu Bachya in parashat Mishpatim that there is grave danger in fish with cheese, and the same with milk — therefore he ruled that even b'dieved it is forbidden; but fish with butter he wrote is permitted since everyone does so — see there. And it appears to me that nowadays since everyone cooks also with milk it is permitted, for since the many have trodden upon it, etc.
10#_: Almond milk. Beit HaTaharah — what Maharshal ruled, etc. And see in Nitzotz that I wrote that nevertheless one should not forbid placing fowl meat in almond milk without placing almonds beside it, except if before viewers as at great feasts where there is full marit ayin; but in one's house it is permitted — see there. And what Beit HaTaharah and Taz wrote, etc. — one should not forbid eating, etc. — Taz implies from his words that the same law applies to domestic animal meat.
11#_: But if it does not have. Eshel Avraham s.k. 16 — what he challenged on Beit Yosef's explanation of entangled in sinews; and see in Shaar HaMelekh chapter 9 Laws of Forbidden Foods what he wrote to establish Mechaber's view — see there.
